decision: Keep the scratch 102M for one bounded instruction-tuning pilot; defer scratch 1B pretraining.
rationale: The existing 102M has completed approximately 2B pretraining tokens but has not received instruction tuning.
The 0/16 routing probe measures one prompt format and decoding setup; it does not establish the model's ultimate capacity after tuning.
Using the approximate 6ND compute model, 1B parameters at the same token count needs 9.78 times the compute.
A 1B/20B-token planning reference needs about 97.79 times the compute of the completed 102M/2B-token run. This is not a universal minimum or a wall-clock/cost estimate.
Measured instruction learning on held-out tasks should precede further GPU spending or a new model-size commitment.
next_work: Expand and validate teacher examples beyond the 32-example seed.
Freeze independent evaluation cases and record the original model's baseline before tuning.
Run a short instruction-tuning pilot on a separate candidate checkpoint, with cloud runtime/billing controls implemented before launch.
Compare complete generations, tool selection, argument correctness and language regressions; validation loss alone is insufficient.
Reassess further spending based on measured gains. Do not infer general intelligence or autonomous training from a narrow routing test.
